acceptanceCriteria: Document/retain actual account-supported CLI model choices separately from desktop tool metadata and refresh on version/capability changes.
A task can fall back to the selected supported model without source/process loss; retain original unsupported400 failure and model/effort reason.
Do not characterize ordinary alias incompatibility as usage exhaustion, Corvint source defect or permission refusal.
body: Observed Codex CLI0.153.2 on2026-10-02: desktop tool metadata advertised gpt-6.1-sol, but launching codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol under the signed-in ChatGPT account exits1 with HTTP400 model not supported. No model turn/source edits occurred; unknown-model fallback metadata warning precedes failure. This is a runtime model availability/routing gap, not proof of a Corvint product defect or provider usage block. Expected task routing to resolve an account-supported CLI model before launching work, keeping desktop and CLI availability distinct. Supported gpt-5.5/medium from the existing handoff is used for the bounded implementation; gpt-6-astra/high already ran the independent reviews. Dedup searches for gpt-6.1-sol/model alias found only unrelated transient-classifier ticket. Evidence retained in Linux availability control builder.log, builder-state/exit.json, unchanged clean-source readback and CLI resume model decision. Native/provider billing/cache telemetry remains NOT_OBSERVED; do not call prompt changes runtime enforcement.
title: Desktop model alias rejected by installed Codex CLI needs runtime routing evidence
